inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: The book-269 term/definition table — the Ethics subsection's consent page: three printed blocks (Informed consent with its four-part process and WIPE exceptions; Consent for minors with its gates and the Sex/Drugs/Rock-and-roll set; Advance directives with its four instrument rows) — the page's only printed asset and the operational core of patient autonomy
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: TWO-COLUMN TERM/DEFINITION TABLE, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read at 120dpi, staging-pubh19/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): the running-header ribbon (PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCES → PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCES—ETHICS, printed ONCE; SECTION II block with page number 269), then the table — bold dark-navy term names on pale light-blue/gray shaded cells in the left column (Informed consent, Consent for minors, Advance directives as the three main, larger terms; Oral advance directive, Written advance directive, Medical power of attorney, Do not resuscitate order as four smaller bold medium-blue sub-rows), definitions in the right column with small square bullet glyphs, thin black horizontal rules, no vertical borders, no zebra striping. RED TEXT (First Aid's own): the heading 'Exceptions to informed consent (WIPE it away):' prints 'WIPE' in red with the four exception bullets led by bold red initial letters — Waiver—patient explicitly relinquishes the right of informed consent; Legally Incompetent—patient lacks decision-making capacity (obtain consent from legal surrogate); Therapeutic Privilege—withholding information when disclosure would severely harm the patient or undermine informed decision-making capacity; Emergency situation—implied consent may apply — and the minors box's 'Sex', 'Drugs', 'Rock and roll' lead words print in bold red: Sex (contraception, STIs, prenatal care—usually not abortion); Drugs (substance use disorder treatment); Rock and roll (emergency/trauma). Also printed: the four process requirements (Disclosure, Understanding, Capacity [distinct from competence, a legal determination], Voluntariness), the comprehensive-understanding sentence (alternative options including no treatment), the revocation clause (revoke written consent at any time, even orally), the minors default (<18 years old; parental consent laws vary by state; emergency treatment eg blood transfusions; legally emancipated eg married, self-supporting, or in the military), the communication and assent closers, the directives lead (instructions given in anticipation; details vary per state law), and the four instrument rows with the POA's 'More flexible than a living will' and the DNR's CPR-only scope. Line-wrap hyphenations in print: 'decision-making' (twice), 'life-sustaining', and 'prenatal care—usually'.
inventory.kypLocation: the whole registry visual (ConsentMap in visuals/pubhealth-p19.tsx, viewBox 0 0 1102 1290), four zones: Zone A the four process pillars in printed order (Disclosure / Understanding / Capacity-with-the-competence-parenthetical / Voluntariness, each with its printed definition) plus the disclosure-set strip (INCLUDING NO TREATMENT) and the revocation strip; Zone B the four WIPE exception cards with red initial letters and First Aid attribution; Zone C the minors panel (the <18 default card, the EMERGENCY TREATMENT and LEGALLY EMANCIPATED gate chips, the attributed red Sex/Drugs/Rock-and-roll row, and the communication + assent closers); Zone D the four advance-directive instruments — Oral / Written / Medical power of attorney as staircase cards on the KYP flexibility ladder (flagged: the print ranks only implicitly, 'More flexible than a living will') with the DNR drawn beside as the scoped CPR-only order; the full page's text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's table block (blocks[1]), core.what, the decoder list block (blocks[2]), and recall[0-7]
